deities: Lakulisha (incarnation/aspect of Lord Shiva; founder of the Pashupata sect)

history.period: 971 AD (per multiple travel/tourism sources - verify; inscription-based confirmation not found in consulted sources)
history.summary: SUB-SHRINE NOTE: The Lakulish Temple is one of the 108 shrines within the Eklingji temple complex (CSV row 2071) - the two CSV rows describe the same complex, with this row being a sub-shrine. It is dated to 971 AD in multiple sources and is described as the only temple of the Lakulisha-Pashupata sect in India (claim widely repeated in travel literature - verify). Lakulisha is the revered founder of the Pashupata tradition, and the Eklingji complex's original affiliation was likely Pashupata, consistent with this shrine's presence. No separate detailed history, dedicated source page, or independently verifiable image of the Lakulish shrine itself was found; coordinates and most visitor details are those of the Eklingji complex (geocode FULL_ADDRESS match 'Jai Ekling Ji, Girwa', relevance 100), flagged as approximate to the complex. The media image shows the Eklingji complex generally, not the Lakulish shrine specifically (verify).

name: Lakulish Temple
town: Eklingji (within the Eklingji complex, village Kailashpuri, ~22 km north of Udaipur)
town_description: The Lakulish Temple stands inside the walled Eklingji temple complex at Kailashpuri village in Udaipur district, about 22 km north of Udaipur on the Nathdwara road. Eklingji is the foremost of Mewar's four major pilgrimage sites, set in an Aravalli valley near Nagda, the old Mewar capital.

travel.airport: Maharana Pratap Airport, Udaipur - about 30 km (verify).
travel.road: Same as the Eklingji complex: about 22 km north of Udaipur via NH-48 (verify).

visitor_information.opening_hours: Same as the Eklingji complex (reported 4:30-7:00 am, 10:30 am-1:30 pm, 5:00-7:30 pm; verify).
